question.leadin: Answer the following about early colonization of the Americas.
question.text: This was the first permanent English settlement in North America, founded in 1607. It nearly succumbed to famine in its early years, but was kept afloat by the leadership of John Smith and Lord De La Warr.
question.clue: The first meeting of the House of Burgesses took place here, and it was burned to the ground during Bacon's Rebellion.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about women in early American history.
swap.text: This religious leader was banished from the Massachusetts Bay Colony for rejecting the "covenant of works" during the Antinomian Controversy and relocated to Rhode Island after her followers were given refuge by Roger Williams.
swap.clue: John Winthrop presided over a trial of this woman, leading Roger Williams to support her founding of Portsmouth, Rhode Island.

question.leadin: The war saw the British under Anson attacking the Manila Galleon, after which he circumnavigated the globe.
question.text: Identify this war that saw the battles at Porto Bello and Cartagena that was sparked by the Spanish seizure of its namesake's ship, Rebecca.
question.clue: Seeing an unsuccessful amphibious assault on Cartagena de Indias, the incident that sparked this war involved the boarding of the ship Rebecca.

swap.leadin: Peter Minuit purchased this landmass from a group of Lenape Native Americans for $24 worth of goods, despite the fact that the land was controlled by other people.
swap.text: Name this island that became part of New Amsterdam.
swap.clue: Its very regular street grid is interrupted by the diagonal crossing of Broadway, which runs nearly the entire length of this island.

question.text: This Virginia Governor's policies incited Bacon's Rebellion. This man was appointed by Charles I and replaced Sir Francis Wyatt.
question.clue: This successor to Francis Wyatt who upset his white constituency by adopting friendlier relations with Native Americans. This governor died before he could explain his actions to King Charles II.

swap.leadin: Everyone likes pirates! Answer these questions about real pirates.
swap.text: In 1718, this man blockaded the port of Charlestown with his ship The Queen Anne's Revenge and two smaller vessels. He allegedly lit fuses around his face to appear more menacing.
swap.clue: This pirate held Samuel Wragg hostage during a blockade of Charleston, during which he demanded a chest of medicine.

question.text: This Quaker founded a colony named for him in 1681, from which Delaware later split off.
question.clue: In an event depicted by a Benjamin West painting, this man expanded his holdings by signing treaties with the Lenape tribe after he was given a colony by Charles II.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about early leaders in New England.
swap.text: This man succeeded John Carver as governor of his colony and detailed its history in Of Plymouth Plantation.
swap.clue: His most notable work chronicles the changing of the name of Mount Wallaston to Merry Mountain.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Native American prophets.
question.text: The prophet Neolin's anti-materialistic messages directly influenced this chieftain, who revolted against Jeffrey Amherst's Indian policies.
question.clue: A reward for this man's death was announced by Jeffrey Amherst.

swap.leadin: Some of the participants in this revolt were upset that Catholic priests had destroyed their kivas, or ceremonial pits.
swap.text: Identify this 1680 rebellion led by a man named Pope (po-PAY) in modern day New Mexico.
swap.clue: This conflict witnessed the death of about 900 members of the Acomans.

question.leadin: Name these players in conflicts between Native Americans and English colonists.
question.text: This son of Massasoit and ruler of the Wampagnoag lends his name to a 1675 to 1676 war which included the massacre of Narrangaset in the Great Swamp Fight.
question.clue: He was slain while trying to avoid Benjamin Church's men while hiding in the Miery Swamp near Mount Hope.

swap.leadin: This man famously said "He who does not work, does not eat."
swap.text: Identify this English explorer known for his role in helping to establish Jamestown.
swap.answerHtml: John Smith [prompt on Smith, no way in hell are we going to give points for just saying “Smith”]
swap.clue: This man was forced to return to England by a gunpowder injury, after negotiating a trade deal with native tribes to help alleviate the Starving Time.

question.leadin: This man sold his stock in the Royal African Company after a letter from the enslaved Job Ben Solomon changed his views on slavery and convinced him to buy Solomon's freedom.
question.text: Name this man who founded a colony intended to resettle the "unemployed and unemployable" of England which initially outlawed slavery.
question.clue: Earlier, this man led a Parliamentary committee on prison reform, which inspired him to found a haven for debtors.

swap.text: Nathaniel Bacon, the leader of his namesake rebellion, was soon thereafter elected to this group, which was the first legislative assembly in the American colonies.
swap.clue: Distinguished members included Captain Francis West and Reverend William Wickham.

question.leadin: Robert Fogel posited one of these periods spanning roughly the 1960s through 80s, though William G. McLoughlin's thesis about the third period of this type is much more widely accepted.
question.text: Name these periods of spiritual revival in America, whose first iteration was exemplified by Jonathan Edwards and George Whitefield.
question.answerHtml: Great Awakenings [accept First, Second, Third, or Fourth Great Awakening]
question.clue: In 1801, over 20,000 people participated in one of these events by attending the Cane Ridge Revival in Kentucky.

swap.text: Along with the Moor Estevanico, Cabeza de Vaca was one of the few survivors of this hurricane-wracked 1527 expedition that crashed on Galveston Island. This expedition besieged the Tocobaga and Apalachee tribes of Florida.

question.leadin: Under leaders like George Durant, this rebellion toppled Albemarle governor Thomas Miller, who escaped from prison in Charles Town and notified the House of Lords.
question.text: Name this 1677 revolt in Carolina against the imposition of the Navigation Acts.
question.clue: Arms for this event were provided by Captain Zachary Gilliam, which started after Valentine Byrd and Timothy Biggs were replaced by Thomas Eastchurch and Thomas Miller to enforce a statute ignored by John Judkins and Governor Drummond.

swap.leadin: Name these things about James Oglethorpe's role in the War of Jenkins' Ear.
swap.text: Oglethorpe's first action was to lead an unsuccessful siege of this Spanish city. It was founded in 1565 by Pedro Menendez, making it the oldest continuously occupied site settled by Europeans in the Americas.
swap.clue: Coquina rock was used to build a bastioned fortress protecting this city, the Castillo de San Marcos, that replaced a cedar-log fort burned by Sir Francis Drake in 1586.

question.leadin: One government passed several pieces of legislation restricting the sexual behavior of these people, such as ones "Against secrett marriage" and "Against ffornication"
question.text: Name these people who gained rights as their behavior became more legislated through the mid-17th century. John Punch is believed to have been one of these people before losing a landmark legal case and his freedom.
question.clue: This people who had to work for a set amount of time- usually either four, five, or seven years- in order to pay for their transport to the New World.

swap.text: Further anti-Andros activity could be seen in New York, where this German-born colonist led a 1689 revolt which deposed Andros' deputy Francis Nicholson. He was eventually executed in 1691 for treason.
swap.clue: The major accomplishment of his two-year-long regime was calling for an attack on Quebec in the first independent congress of the North American colonies.
